is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on the malaria vector Anopheles funestus (Title, Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes the L119F-GSTe2 mutation (Abstract, Page 1; Section 2.6, Page 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype frequencies and sample sizes are provided in Figures 3, 4, and 5, and Table 7 (e.g., '40 alive vs. 40 dead' for Olyset Plus cone assays).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Mibellon, a village in the Adamawa Region of Cameroon (Section 2.1, Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting experimental hut trials and molecular genotyping results.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to Mibellon village, Mayo Banyo Division, Adamawa Region, Cameroon (Section 2.1, Page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted between 10 July and 16 October 2016 (Section 2.1, Page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the authors have published other studies from Mibellon, this paper describes a specific experimental hut trial conducted in 2016 with its own unique dataset.

supplement.evidence: The paper refers to Supplementary Materials (Figure S1, Tables S1-S3) available online which contain additional data on exophily, mortality, and blood feeding (Page 18).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of PBO-based (PermaNet 3.0, Olyset Plus) and pyrethroid-only (PermaNet 2.0, Olyset) LLINs against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles funestus in Mibellon, Cameroon. Using experimental huts and WHO cone/tube assays, the authors demonstrated that GST-mediated metabolic resistance (specifically the GSTe2 L119F marker) significantly impacts the performance of these nets, affecting mortality, blood-feeding success, and exophily.
